rel_l2_note: Per-seed relative_l2_error UNIFORM 3.99e-7 across all 5 seeds (captured via runs/dump_metrics.py, which surfaces multi_seed_correctness.per_seed_results; verify.py gates on l2_norm_passed but does not print the numeric value). ~50x under the 2e-5 gate. NOTE: the profiler's MultiSeedCorrectnessResult.all_seeds_passed=False aggregates the COMPOSITE CorrectnessResult.passed (allclose-prioritized, models.py:469-480), NOT l2_norm_passed; NKIBench and verify.py gate on l2_norm_passed (True all seeds) -> verify.py reported PASS (correct 1/1). This is the documented allclose-vs-relative-L2 distinction (CLAUDE.md).
structure: M-block-outer streaming GEMM, NO explicit transpose stage. Layout: NKIBench transform_to_nki_inputs reshapes lhs (2048,4096)->v1 (128,16,4096) and rhs (2048,10944)->v2 (128,16,10944); the reshape maps flat k = k_in*16 + kt so the contraction K sits on the PARTITION axis of BOTH operands. nisa.nc_matmul(stationary, moving) = stationary.T @ moving with contraction on the partition axis of both, so feeding stationary=lhs_blk[:,kt,128*s:128*s+128] ([k_in=128,m_sub=128]) and moving=rhs_chunk[:,kt,:] ([k_in=128,n=456]) yields [m_sub,456], PSUM-accumulated over the 16 kt tiles to reconstruct K=2048 -- the transposed-lhs operand is a free byproduct of the input layout (same idiom the NKIBench baseline uses). Constants M_TILES=32 K_TILES=16 M_BLK=8 M_BLOCKS=4 N_CHUNK=456 N_CHUNKS=24. 4 m-blocks of 1024 rows: lhs_blk [128,16,1024] fp32 (64KB/part) loaded ONCE/block, resident; rhs streamed in N_CHUNK=456 chunks ([128,16,456], ~28.5KB/part) reused across the 8 subtiles => rhs re-read 4x total (once/block), not 32x. Per subtile: zero-init [128,456] fp32 PSUM bank, 16-tile kt nc_matmul PSUM accumulation, single PSUM->SBUF nl.copy, single SBUF->HBM nl.store. Output index: out[8*mb+s, mi, 456*c+nj] -> logical row m = mb*1024 + s*128 + mi (v3 (32,128,10944) reshapes to (4096,10944)).
n_chunk_choice: N_CHUNK=456 = exact divisor of N=10944 (456*24) AND <=512 (one fp32 PSUM bank width) => every tile full-size, ZERO tail-masking arithmetic anywhere. The NKIBench baseline uses N_CHUNK=1024 (2x512 PSUM banks) WITH mask=...>=0 tail bounds on load/matmul/copy/store; this kernel deliberately replaces that to remove the single largest correctness-bug surface. ~2% free-axis under-fill vs 512 is a phase-2/3 concern, not phase-1.
numeric_path: fp32 end-to-end: every nl.load / PSUM accumulator (nl.zeros) / nl.copy / nl.store is np.float32; no dtype cast (no bf16/narrowing) anywhere. PSUM (Tensor-Engine) accumulation via acc[...] += nc_matmul(...) over 16 kt tiles; exactly one PSUM->SBUF copy + one store per output tile (no PSUM->SBUF round trips).
hbm_model: HBMrd 392.2MB EXACT = lhs 2048*4096*4=33.55MB x1 + rhs 2048*10944*4=89.65MB x4 (once per m-block). HBMwr 179.3MB EXACT = out 4096*10944*4=179.3MB x1. No spill (psum_read_sbuf_write_count=768 = 4*24*8 = one drain per output tile; HBM at the once-lhs/4x-rhs/once-out floor).
dominant_engine: PE (Tensor Engine) = 99.8%, TRUE PE-active 4.718ms ~= p50 4.727ms. PE-BOUND at the fp32 systolic floor (MFU 49% = the bf16-peak-denominator structural cap on a correct fp32 GEMM, not inefficiency; BL-20260709-fp32-pe-floor-calibration). DEC-2 diagnostic recorded; PE-dominance CONFIRMED (validates the compute-bound hypothesis, sets the phase-2 lever).
notes: First correct Phase-1 kernel for transpose_matmul; correctness-first goal met on first implementation attempt (no correctness iteration needed -- the layout mapping was already proven by the NKIBench baseline's same no-transpose nc_matmul-over-16-kt idiom). fp32, full 5-seed L2 PASS (rel-L2 3.99e-7 ~50x under gate), 1.026x over the 4.849615ms baseline (already beats baseline; far inside the resolved DEC-1 soft <=1.5x ceiling). PE-bound at the fp32 floor with DMA fully hidden and HBM exactly at the ~4x-rhs model (no spill). Built on the explicit nc_matmul idiom so the Phase-2 compensated bf16x2 split is a localized matmul-only change, not a rewrite. Phase-2 reference: the lever is COMPUTE (the fp32 PE floor); candidate is the compensated bf16x2 3-product split, to be MEASURED against the recorded 2.0-instr/site emulation cost (same count that LOST on swiglu but WON on the matmul_add_rmsnorm siblings; the sign depends on the per-instruction fp32 rate on this large moving-456 GEMM + weight residency -- BL-20260710-bf16x2-loses-when-fp32-emulates-in-2-passes). See profile/tmm_v1_digest.md and profile/tmm_v1_dump.txt.

rel_l2_note: On-device per-seed relative_l2_error UNIFORM 4.451495e-6 across all 5 seeds (l2_norm_passed=True every seed; captured via runs/dump_metrics.py). ~4.5x under the 2e-5 gate. Quadrature corroboration (AC-2.1): backed-out bf16 term sqrt(ondevice^2 - floor^2) = sqrt(4.4515e-6^2 - 3.99e-7^2) = 4.4336e-6 == offline 3-product 4.452e-6 within 0.41% -- the 3.99e-7 fp32 floor (from tmm_v1) is negligible under the root, so device rel-L2 ~= the bf16 term (pure-GEMM regime, NOT the add_rmsnorm ~1.46e-5 family). NOTE all_seeds_passed=False is the allclose-vs-relativeL2 distinction (verify.py/NKIBench gate on l2_norm_passed=True); documented in tmm_v1.
structure: Compensated bf16x2 3-product split of BOTH operands; LOCALIZED matmul-only diff on tmm_v1. Loop nest, constants (M_TILES=32 K_TILES=16 M_BLK=8 M_BLOCKS=4 N_CHUNK=456 N_CHUNKS=24), fp32 PSUM accumulation over 16 kt, and single copy+store epilogue are byte-for-byte tmm_v1; only the operand dtype path changes. Per m-block: build lhs_hi/lhs_lo bf16 [128,16,1024] (2x32KB=64KB/part = same bytes as v1 fp32 lhs_blk) resident from the fp32 loads. Per (mb,c): build rhs_hi/rhs_lo bf16 [128,16,456] (2x~14.25KB~=28.5KB/part = same as v1 fp32 rhs_chunk), reused across 8 subtiles. Inner: 1 fp32 nc_matmul replaced by 3 bf16 nc_matmul (hi@hi, hi@lo, lo@hi, FIXED order, dropping lo@lo) into one fp32 PSUM bank. Limb build: nl.copy(dtype=bfloat16) RNE for hi, nisa.tensor_tensor(op=nl.subtract) fp32 residual then nl.copy for lo. NO explicit transpose (lhs arrives K-on-partition), NO PSUM round-trip for limbs, NO transpose scratch -- simpler than the matmul_add_rmsnorm sibling which transposes x per tile.
offline_gate: runs/offline_bf16_split_sim.py (pure GEMM, no z/g/norm): fp32 control vs numpy reference = 0.000e+00 (bit-exact, validates seed/draw-order/dtype/formula); worst bf16x2 3-product rel-L2 = 4.453e-6 over seeds {42,0,21,63,84,123,2024}; 4-product 3.492e-6 (dropped lo@lo ~1e-6, D4 unnecessary); plain bf16 2.350e-3 (scale check). predicted device quadrature sqrt(3.99e-7^2 + 4.453e-6^2) = 4.471e-6 << 2e-5. Comfortably below (<1.3e-5) => authorized the build.

Mechanism: 2.0 fp32 passes x1.95 = 3.90 -> 3.0 bf16-equiv = -23% PE-active.
hbm_spill_check: NO SPILL. hbm_write_bytes 179306496 (179.3MB) BYTE-IDENTICAL to v1; psum_read_sbuf_write_count 768 BYTE-IDENTICAL to v1 -- the two definitive spill signatures both absent. hbm_read_bytes 392167424->447832064 (+14.2%, +55.7MB): input-reload read traffic from the compiler's software pipeline under the added SBUF pressure of resident bf16 limbs + transient fp32 build scratch (NOT an evict/reload of intermediates, which would show in write/psum). DMA stays fully hidden (37% << PE 94%), so it costs zero wall-clock. Documented deviation from AC-4's ~392MB read expectation; not a spill, not a rejection (wall-clock authority per AC-5).
dominant_engine: PE (Tensor Engine) = 93.66%, still PE-dominant but NOT saturated at the fp32 floor (was 99.8%). TRUE PE-active 3.626ms ~= p50 3.87ms. MFU 45% (bf16-mix). The split lifted the fp32 systolic floor -23% while limb-build Vec/Scl (5->19%, 0->12%) and the +14% DMA remain hidden under PE.
levers_not_run: D4 (4-product): SKIPPED -- offline worst 3-product 4.453e-6 << 1.8e-5 danger band, numerically unnecessary. D3 (M_BLK sweep): NOT run -- DMA remained fully hidden (37% << PE 94%), no basis to move a PE-bound wall; flagged possible anti-lever (BL-20260710-cross-batch-blocking-is-an-antilever-on-affine-range). Available as a follow-up screen composed on tmm_v2 if a further push is wanted.

Compensated bf16x2 3-product split, MEASURED (not assumed) per BL-20260710-bf16x2-loses-when-fp32-emulates-in-2-passes. SECOND WIN at 2.0-matmul-instr/site (after matmul_add_rmsnorm 4.879x) confirming the count is a SCREEN not a verdict: the sign is set by the per-instruction fp32 rate (measured 1.95x here) + limb residency (2x bf16 = 1x fp32 bytes, no reload trap) -- both swiglu-loss conditions absent. tmm_v1 kept unchanged as the guaranteed pure-fp32 fallback. archive_reason: Correct + real wall win (1.253x, RAW PE-active -23.0%) but FAILS AC-4: full-run hbm_read_bytes 447832064 (447.8MB) = +14.2% over v1's 392MB no-growth floor. Root cause: compiler software pipeline re-fetches ~15% of rhs input tiles under the larger resident bf16-limb working set at M_BLK=8 (the two spill signatures hbm_write_bytes=179306496 + psum_read_sbuf_write_count=768 are byte-identical to v1, so NOT an intermediate spill). structure: tmm_v2 with the low bf16 limb produced DIRECTLY by the residual subtract writing into a bf16 destination (fused), removing the separate fp32 residual buffer + one copy. Intended to shrink the limb-build working set and cut v2's HBM-read growth.
notes: Diagnostic: byte-IDENTICAL to tmm_v2 on EVERY metric (hbm_read 447832064, write 179306496, psum 768, matmul 36864, vec 3000, scl 2734). The compiler already casts the tensor_tensor subtract result to the destination dtype at no cost, so fusing the lo-limb is a no-op -- proving the +14.2% read growth is NOT from the separate fp32 residual buffer but from rhs re-fetch under the M_BLK=8 working set (fixed by M_BLK=16 in tmm_v3). Not promoted; recorded as first-class negative evidence for the AC-4 root-cause. See BL-20260710-compiler-copy-propagates-exact-psum-sbuf-copy.

rel_l2_note: Full-5-seed per-seed relative_l2_error UNIFORM 4.451495e-6 (l2_norm_passed=True every seed), IDENTICAL to tmm_v2/v2b/v4 -- the bf16x2 split arithmetic is unchanged; only the M-block tiling differs. Quadrature back-out sqrt(4.4515e-6^2 - 3.99e-7^2)=4.4336e-6 == offline 4.452e-6 within 0.41%. ~4.5x under the 2e-5 gate.
structure: tmm_v2_bf16_split with M_BLK=16 (2 blocks of 2048 rows) instead of M_BLK=8 (4 blocks of 1024). rhs is re-streamed once per M-block, so the rhs read multiple = block count: 2 blocks => rhs read x2 (was x4). Resident lhs bf16 limbs [128,16,2048] x2 = 128KB/partition; rhs limbs [128,16,456] x2 ~= 28.5KB; transient fp32 build tiles small; peak ~168KB/part < 192KB (no spill). Low limb produced directly by nisa.tensor_tensor(op=subtract) into a bf16 destination (exact fp32 residual internally, downcast free -- no separate fp32 residual buffer). 3 bf16 products hi@hi+hi@lo+lo@hi in one fp32 PSUM bank, dropping lo@lo. Epilogue (copy PSUM->SBUF fp32, store) unchanged. N_CHUNK=456 (exact divisor, no tail mask).
hbm_ac4: AC-4 PASS. Full-run hbm_read_bytes 228970496 (229.0MB) = -41.6% vs v1's 392.2MB floor (rhs read multiple halved 4x->2x). hbm_write_bytes 179306496 (179.3MB) + psum_read_sbuf_write_count 768 BYTE-IDENTICAL to v1 (no spill). Resolves v2's +14.2% read regression.
speed_analysis: Same-session bracket v1a->v3->v2->v1b (--fast): v1 4.7275/4.7271 (band 0.0085%); v3 p50 3.6358ms beats v1 (worse anchor) by 23.1% >> max(band,3%)=0.1418ms, and beats the v2 branch (3.8699) by 6.0%. DMA 37%(v2)->22%(v3), so the previously-marginal DMA exposure at M_BLK=8 is now fully hidden -- that plus the halved rhs reads is the 6% gain over v2. Full-5-seed p50 3.6338ms, PE 98%. RAW tensor_engine_active_time_ns 9431025(v1)->7126656(v3) = -24.4% (window-independent; v1 anchors agree 0.002%); vs v2 7262192 = -1.9% (v3 slightly lower PE-active too).
lever: D3/M_BLK lever ADOPTED. Gated in per AC-7 (D1=v2 shifted the DMA balance off hidden 21%->37%, and the read growth was the AC-4 problem, so screening M_BLK was licensed). It WON rather than being the flagged anti-lever (BL-20260710-cross-batch-blocking-is-an-antilever-on-affine-range) because it CUTS the rhs read multiple (a real traffic reduction) rather than enlarging a cross-iteration resident live set that constrains the pipeline; the 128KB/part resident lhs limbs still fit with no spill and PE returned to 98%.
notes: PROMOTED at 1.334x -- first transpose_matmul kernel to beat v1's 1.026x, and the phase-2 kernel of record. Same compensated bf16x2 3-product split as tmm_v2 (correctness identical) but M_BLK=16 fixes v2's AC-4 read regression (229MB << 392MB floor) AND is 6% faster. THIRD (cleanest) WIN at 2.0-matmul-instr/site after matmul_add_rmsnorm -- a pure GEMM isolating the mechanism (per-instruction fp32 rate 1.95x bf16; 1.5/1.95=0.769 == measured -24% PE-active). rel_l2_note: rel-L2 4.4515e-6 (seed 42, l2_norm_passed=True), identical to v3 -- split arithmetic unchanged.
structure: tmm_v3_mblk16 with N tiled as 21 full 512-wide chunks + one 192-wide tail chunk (22 chunk-groups vs 24 at N_CHUNK=456). Tail is a SEPARATE narrow chunk (192 is a valid moving width <=512), NOT a padded-to-512 masked chunk -- correct-by-construction, does less matmul work than pad+mask, and avoids the tail-mask off-by-one bug surface. Same limb build + 3-product body for full and tail chunks.
speed_analysis: Same-session bracket v3a->v4->v3b (--fast): v3 band 0.0055%; v4 p50 3.6762ms REGRESSES +1.12% vs v3 3.6353ms (>> band). matmul_instruction_count 36864->33792 (-8.3%) and psum 768->704, but TRUE PE-active RISES 3.564->3.575ms and hbm_read 229->257MB. The -8% instruction saving does NOT convert to PE-active: the kernel is PE-COLUMN-bound (the total PE columns pushed are ~the same), not issue-overhead-bound, and the 192-wide tail under-fills.
notes: MEASURED REJECT. D2 (N_CHUNK=512+192 tail) is correct and cuts matmul instructions -8.3% but the wall REGRESSES +1.12% outside the same-session band (exactly the AC-7 negative test: adopting D2 on an instruction-count improvement alone without a real wall win). tmm_v3_mblk16 stays promoted. See profile/tmm_phase2r1_d2_*.txt, profile/tmm_phase2r1_v4_nchunk512_fast.txt.

rel_l2_note: rel-L2 4.4515e-6 (seed 42, l2_norm_passed=True), identical to v3 -- split arithmetic unchanged. The MASKED-tail path is correct: hbm_write_bytes 179306496 EXACT (the store mask prevents the 320 out-of-range columns of the last chunk from writing beyond out[.,.,10944]).
structure: tmm_v3_mblk16 with the plan-exact N_CHUNK=512 MASKED-tail tiling (NOT tmm_v4's separate-narrow-tail): N=10944 -> 22 uniform 512-wide chunks (ceil(10944/512)); valid_n = (N-1)-(512*c+inc) >= 0 masks the last chunk's 320 out-of-range columns (10944..11263). rhs LOAD is masked (invalid lanes zero -> zero bf16 limbs -> zero matmul contribution over the full 512 columns, no separate tail path), output STORE is masked (no OOB write). Mirrors the NKIBench baseline mask idiom. Split/product order/PSUM/epilogue identical to v3.
speed_analysis: Same-session bracket v3a->v5->v3b (--fast): v3 band 0.0138%; v5 p50 3.7887ms REGRESSES +4.2% vs v3 3.6362ms (>> band). matmul_instruction_count 36864->33792 (-8.3%), psum 768->704, BUT TRUE PE-active RISES 3.564->3.678ms (+3.2%) and hbm_read 229->253MB. WORSE than the mask-free separate-tail v4 (+1.12%): the tail-mask arithmetic on load+store adds overhead ON TOP OF the wider-chunk non-benefit.
notes: MEASURED REJECT -- the plan-EXACT masked-tail form of D2 (Codex round-1 review asked for this specific implementation, not tmm_v4's mask-free narrow tail). Correct (mask boundary works, no OOB write) and cuts matmul instructions -8.3%, but the wall REGRESSES +4.2% outside the band, and it is worse than the mask-free variant -- so the mask arithmetic itself costs, exactly as the plan warned when it noted phase-1 deliberately removed the mask. D2 now rejected in BOTH forms (mask-free v4 +1.12%, masked v5 +4.2%); the kernel is PE-column-bound, not issue-overhead-bound, so fewer/wider chunks cannot help. tmm_v3_mblk16 stays promoted at 1.334x. See profile/tmm_phase2r2_v3a.txt, tmm_phase2r2_v5.txt, tmm_phase2r2_v3b.txt.

rel_l2_note: rel-L2 4.4515e-6 (seed 42, l2_norm_passed=True), IDENTICAL to v3 -- the bf16x2 3-product split arithmetic is unchanged; only the rhs-limb build chunk width differs. Bit-exact reschedule, so no offline re-derivation needed (AC-5).
lever: E1 (phase-3 gap-only): widen the rhs bf16-limb BUILD chunk 456->912 to HALVE the number of limb-build prologues (12/M-block vs 24), attacking the limb-build-prologue component of the ~2% PE-idle gap.
structure: tmm_v3_mblk16 with N_BUILD=912 (12 build chunks, exact divisor 912*12) for the rhs-limb build, and the 16 subtiles matmul'd in TWO 456-wide sub-chunks per build chunk (912=456*2). CLEAN ISOLATION: matmul moving width stays 456 (the proven-good, exact-divisor, mask-free width), so matmul_instruction_count, PSUM-bank usage, and PE column count are byte-identical to tmm_v3 (36864); the ONLY changed variable is the rhs-limb build granularity. This is NOT tmm_v4/v5's chunk-WIDTH change (N_CHUNK 456->512 + tail), which was already measured-rejected as a PE-column non-benefit.
speed_analysis: Same-session bracket v3a->v6->v3b (--fast): v3 control band |v3a-v3b| = 0.03% wall (3.6355 vs 3.6365) / 0.08% PE-active (3.5630 vs 3.5658). v6 p50 7.3303ms REGRESSES +101.6% vs v3 3.6355ms (~1000x the band). TRUE PE-active/inf RISES 3.5630->4.0458ms (+13.5%) -- immediate-reject signal (PE-active must never rise). Rejected on all three gates simultaneously: wall >> max(band,3%), PE-active rising, AND AC-4 (read+spill) blown.
hbm_ac4: AC-4 FAIL (both signatures). hbm_read 228970496->1764706304 (229->1765MB, 7.7x) AND hbm_write 179306496->259588096 (179.3->259.6MB, +45% = 80MB of spill saves). psum_read_sbuf_write_count stayed 768 (the PSUM drain count is unchanged; the spill is bf16-limb SBUF eviction to HBM, which shows in hbm_write not psum). This is a hard AC-4 rejection independent of the wall.
root_cause: The 912-wide rhs limbs are 2x[128,16,912] bf16 = 2*(16*912*2) = 58368 B/part ~= 57KB (vs v3's 28.5KB at 456). On top of the 128KB/part resident lhs bf16 limbs + transient fp32 build scratch, peak SBUF exceeds the ~192KB trn2 budget, so the compiler spills the bf16 limbs to HBM and re-fetches them (hbm_write +80MB spill, hbm_read explodes 7.7x, DMA 22.5->39%, PE falls 98->55%). Enlarged-resident-live-set anti-lever, same class as BL-20260710-cross-batch-blocking-is-an-antilever-on-affine-range, measured directly on this op. The 'halved prologue count' never mattered because v3's limb build is ALREADY fully hidden (Vec 13.7%/Scl 6.7%/GpSimd 14.2%/DMA 22.5% all << PE 98%).
notes: MEASURED REJECT. E1 is the phase-3 wider-chunk lever in its prologue-count-isolated form (halve the rhs-limb builds without touching matmul width). It regressed catastrophically (+101.6% wall) by spilling the enlarged bf16-limb working set -- confirming the kernel cannot be helped by holding a wider resident limb set. tmm_v3_mblk16 stays promoted at 1.334x (within 3.76% of the 1.385x hard ceiling). See profile/tmm_phase3_v6_nchunk912.txt, tmm_phase3_v3a.txt, tmm_phase3_v3b.txt, docs/phase3-exit-decision.md.

rel_l2_note: rel-L2 4.4515e-6 (seed 42, l2_norm_passed=True), IDENTICAL to v3 -- pure reschedule (two fixed rhs-limb sets A/B + primed build-ahead prefetch), 3-product arithmetic unchanged. matmul_instruction_count 36864 == v3.
disposition: REJECT (measured; faithful build-ahead/prefetch schedule per Codex R1 review, reworked from the R1 build-both-then-matmul batch)
lever: E2 (double-buffer / PREFETCH rhs limbs): TWO fixed rhs-limb buffer sets (A/B) per M-block; prime A<-chunk0, then for p=0..10 build B<-2p+1 (prefetch), matmul A(2p), build A<-2p+2 (prefetch), matmul B(2p+1); final pair build B<-23, matmul A(22), matmul B(23). Straight-line Python-unrolled emission (NOT sequential_range) so each build-ahead can overlap the preceding chunk's matmul.
structure: Fork of tmm_v3_mblk16 with two FIXED resident rhs-limb sets (rhs_hi_a/lo_a, rhs_hi_b/lo_b), each [128,16,456] bf16, both live for the whole M-block N-sweep. M_BLK=16, N_CHUNK=456, 3 bf16 products, output layout and mask-free tiling unchanged. Bit-exact reschedule. This is the FAITHFUL prefetch schedule (build next while matmul-ing current); an earlier R1 version built both chunks of a pair before either matmul (a two-set batch) -- Codex R1 review required this rework.
speed_analysis: Same-session bracket v3a->v7->v3b (--fast): v3 control band |v3a-v3b| = 0.011% wall (3.6356 vs 3.6352) / 0.03% PE-active (3.5643 vs 3.5632). v7 p50 3.6256ms is 0.27% FASTER than v3 mean 3.6354 (outside the 0.011% band -- the prefetch genuinely overlapped a sliver of limb-build with matmul, TRUE PE-active 3.5567ms is -0.2% vs v3), BUT the 0.27% wall gain is FAR below the max(band,3%)=3% adopt threshold and lands inside the ~2% PE-idle-gap ceiling. NOT adoptable on the wall margin, AND rejected on AC-4 (below).
hbm_ac4: AC-4 FAIL (both signatures broken). hbm_read 228970496->283369472 (229->283.4MB, +23.8%): the two fixed resident limb sets enlarge the live working set enough to induce rhs INPUT re-fetch (the tmm_v2 M_BLK=8 448MB class, larger than the R1 batch v7's 257MB because both sets are now live for the whole N-sweep, not just within a pair). hbm_write 179306496->183042048 (179.3->183.0MB, +2.1%): a SMALL WRITE-SPILL (unlike the R1 batch v7 and the promoted v3, whose write was byte-identical 179.3MB) -- the prefetch's longer-lived double buffer tips a little bf16-limb SBUF eviction. psum_read_sbuf_write_count stays 768. Either signature alone rejects under the immutable AC-4 (hbm_read<=229 AND hbm_write==179.3 AND psum==768).
root_cause: The faithful prefetch DOES overlap a sliver of the (Vec/Scl) limb build with the (PE) matmul -- PE-active dips -0.2% and wall -0.27% -- because two fixed buffers let the compiler start chunk c+1's build during chunk c's matmul. But (a) the overlap is tiny: v3's limb build was ALREADY 86% hidden (Vec 13.7%/Scl 6.7%/GpSimd 14.2%/DMA 22.5% all << PE 98%), so there was little exposed build to recover, and the 0.27% wall gain is well inside the ~2% PE-idle-gap ceiling and far under the 3% adopt bar; and (b) holding BOTH limb sets resident for the whole N-sweep enlarges the live working set more than the R1 pair-local batch did, breaking the AC-4 read floor (283MB) AND tipping a small write-spill (183MB). Net: the double-buffer's intended mechanism works but is not worth its memory cost -- the enlarged-resident-live-set anti-lever, now with the prefetch actually engaged.
notes: MEASURED REJECT (faithful build-ahead/prefetch, reworked per Codex R1 review from the R1 batch version). The prefetch engaged (PE-active -0.2%, wall -0.27% outside the 0.011% band) but the wall gain is << the 3% adopt threshold AND it breaks the immutable AC-4 read floor (hbm_read 283.4MB > 229) with a small write-spill (183.0MB > 179.3) -- exactly the tmm_v2 M_BLK=8 situation (faster-but-read-floor-breaking is rejected on AC-4, a real wall win cannot waive the immutable gate). tmm_v3_mblk16 stays PROMOTED at 1.334x (within 3.76% of the 1.385x hard ceiling).
